discovery_mechanism: Each rendered event container in the homepage's EventON calendar (id="event_{event_id}", itemscope itemtype='http://schema.org/Event') carries both the stable data-event_id attribute (see docs/sources/HOT_CLUBE.md's original ICS proof) AND, within that same container, inline Schema.org Event microdata whose <a itemprop='url' href='...'> is that event's own intended individual permalink. This record set extracts that href verbatim from the exact container matching each retained event_id — never slugified or guessed from the title.

permalink_verification.method: Sequential HTTP GET against each of the 9 permalinks above, first-party hcp.pt only, bounded, with a standard browser User-Agent used for one representative re-check to rule out UA-based bot handling.

requests_made.note: re-checked with a standard browser User-Agent (Chrome/124.0); identical 301/Location, confirming this is a genuine server-issued redirect (Apache), not UA-based bot handling

permalink_verification.finding: Every one of the 9 permalinks returns HTTP 301 Moved Permanently with Location: https://hcp.pt/#clube (the Hot Clube homepage's 'clube' anchor) — none resolve to distinct individual-event content. This is a genuine, server-issued redirect (Apache), confirmed with a standard browser User-Agent, not a bot-detection artifact of this proof's own request headers. Consequently none of these permalinks are used as Observation.event_url in this task: doing so would present the source's own homepage as though it were an individual event page.
